summary.tldr: Makes the Auditor General of Canada one of the Bank of Canada’s auditors and updates related federal laws.
what_it_does: Makes the Auditor General of Canada and an accounting firm the Bank of Canada’s auditors.
Lets the Governor in Council appoint, on the minister’s recommendation, a qualified accounting firm to audit the bank.
Keeps the rule that appointed accounting firms serve five fiscal years and cannot be appointed for two straight terms.
Updates the Auditor General Act so its definition of "registrar" includes the Bank of Canada.
Replaces the Bank of Canada exemption in the Financial Administration Act with a version that keeps listed sections from applying to the bank.
summary.background: The Bank of Canada Act already provides for audits by a firm of accountants. This bill adds the Auditor General of Canada as another auditor and makes matching changes in two other Acts.
